_comment: Bring-your-own-corpus benchmark ground truth. Each key is a target the Aegis Vanguard scanner will run against. `expected_findings` are the known-vulnerable defects the scanner SHOULD detect; the judge maps produced findings against them to compute recall/precision. `setup.docker` is optional guidance for standing the target up locally. Only scan targets you are authorized to test.

setup.note: OWASP Juice Shop — intentionally vulnerable Node/Angular app.

expected_findings.description: SQL injection in the login form allows authentication bypass ('  or 1=1--).
DOM XSS via the product search 'q' parameter reflected into the page.
IDOR: a user can access another user's basket by changing the id.
Broken access control exposes the admin section to non-admin users.

setup.note: Damn Vulnerable Web Application — set security level to low.

expected_findings.description: Classic SQL injection in the 'id' GET parameter.
OS command injection in the ping utility 'ip' field.
Local file inclusion via the 'page' parameter.
CSRF on the change-password form (no anti-CSRF token).

setup.note: OWASP WebGoat — deliberately insecure Java teaching app.

expected_findings.description: SQL injection lessons expose injectable query parameters.
XML external entity processing in the comment upload.
Insecure Java deserialization leading to code execution.

setup.note: OWASP NodeGoat — vulnerable Node/Express app (OWASP Top 10).

expected_findings.description: NoSQL injection in the login handler via crafted JSON body.
Server-side JS injection via eval on contribution amounts.
IDOR exposes other users' allocation data by userId.
Stored XSS in profile fields (first/last name).
